In this case, we have to use the identity  $1+{cot}^{2}⁡x={csc}^{2}⁡x.$ Substituting this into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+{cot}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x(1+{cot}^{2}⁡x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x{csc}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
